lead.headline: The Second-Best Team In This League Is 4-4, And Last Wednesday He Stopped Waiting For The Arithmetic To Rescue Him
lead.dek: barringinjury has the second-best all-play record in the Cartel and the worst luck figure in it. On 28 October he sent his own 2027 first to Lovely Day for D’Andre Swift and Darren Waller, five days before scoring 165.62 and losing by 9.38.
body: THE CARTEL — There is a version of this league in which 100 Yards And Runnin is running away with the East. He has scored 1,192.48 points, third most of the twelve. He has beaten sixty-four of the eighty-eight opponents he could theoretically have faced, a figure bettered only by the team that just beat him. He is 4-4.

Nobody in the Cartel is further from the record he has earned. The model puts his expected wins at 5.82 and his luck at minus 1.82, which is to say that two games have gone to the other roster on days when almost any other opponent would have lost. In Week 6 this paper looked at that number and told him to do nothing, on the grounds that luck of that kind returns on its own. It has not returned. He is a game further behind than he was.

So on the Wednesday after that issue he stopped waiting. The deal that cleared at 4.17pm Eastern sent Jordan Watkins and his own 2027 first-round pick to Lovely Day, and brought back D’Andre Swift and Darren Waller. It is the first trade of the season in which a team above .500 has paid a first-round pick for men aged 27 and 34, and it is the clearest statement of intent anybody has made since the summer.

The valuation desk, working to its Week 4 table, prices Swift at 2.41 points a week above replacement. It does not price Waller at all — at 34 he has aged off the bottom of the curve — and it does not price Watkins either. It prices a first-round pick one year out at 1.52. By that arithmetic barringinjury came out 23 percent ahead on the deal, which is the sort of margin the desk would normally reject as too wide to propose. He is also the one who gave up a pick he will not be able to buy back.

What the table cannot see is the hole. His running backs have produced 193.80 points in starting lineups this season, tenth of the twelve. His receivers are third and his tight ends are first in the league. Swift does not have to be good to help; he has to be better than the tenth-best backfield in a twelve-team league, and the number says he is.

Sunday was then a very precise kind of cruelty. He filed 165.62 points, the second-highest total of his season. His roster was capable of 195.98 — the highest ceiling any manager carried into the week — so he converted 84.5 percent of it, which in most weeks wins comfortably. COME AND TAKE IT scored 175.00 at 96.3 percent and beat him by 9.38. That is nine of the twelve teams he would have beaten with the same lineup.

He is still 75.2 percent to qualify and 32.7 percent to take the East, which is the thing worth holding on to. Hoya Paranoia sits above him at 5-3 and 94.1 percent, having just posted a season-low 105.38 of its own. Two of the four teams in that division are mathematically finished in all but name: Trade Calculator Guy at 0.8 percent and Too High Safeties at nought.

The other half of the trade deserves its own sentence, because it is the first sensible thing Lovely Day has done in a month. deucebrat is 3-5, 0.1 percent to qualify, and dead last on the dynasty board at 14.88. He had two useful veterans on a roster that is going nowhere, and the paper said so in last Tuesday’s Notebook — sell Swift. He sold Swift. He now owns two 2027 first-round picks, his own and the one belonging to the team currently fourth in the power rankings, and the pick ledger that read nine-of-twelve-in-two-hands a fortnight ago now has five names on it.
There is one more thing to say about the week, and it is not about football.

Editor’s note on this issue’s box scores. Sleeper settled Week 8 in the standings on Tuesday morning and then did not finish the job. Its per-week record for Week 8 still reports 0.00 for nine men who played — Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Lamar Jackson, Caleb Williams, Cooper Kupp, Luther Burden, D’Andre Swift, Zach Charbonnet, Tre Tucker and AJ Barner, none of them on a bye — and the twelve team totals in that file come to 95.58 points less than the league’s own season figures. Every score, record, roster ceiling and efficiency percentage you read below is correct: they are reconciled from the cumulative totals Sleeper did settle, which balance to the cent, points for against points against, at 12,315.00 apiece. What is missing is the layer underneath. There are no individual lines for Week 8, no Start/Sit Desk, no named benchings and no roster-by-roster box score, and they will not appear until the league rewrites the week. A paper with a hole in it is better than a paper that tells eleven managers Smith-Njigba scored nothing.

notebook.title: Football Morning in the Cartel
intro: I spent Sunday evening watching a spreadsheet refuse to agree with itself, which is not how I had planned to spend it, and I have come out of the experience with more sympathy for the people who keep score for a living. Somewhere in a server this week, nine football players who went out and earned their money were recorded as having scored nothing at all. The league table knew better. The page underneath it did not.

It made me think about how much of what we argue about in this league is really an argument about bookkeeping. A man loses by 9.38 and we say he was unlucky. A man wins by 60 and we say he is a contender. Both of those are stories we tell on top of a number somebody typed in.
Anyway. There was football, and it was the best week of it we have had.

signoff.label: One last thing
signoff.text: The man who is second in this league on every measure except the one that counts spent a first-round pick on Wednesday to stop being told to be patient. I have watched a lot of people in this sport decide that waiting was cowardice. Usually they are wrong. Occasionally the arithmetic really is never coming, and the only way to find out which it was is to look at this page in January.

rumors.title: Charles Robinson’s Notebook
rumors.byline: Charles Robinson · Not F*cking Around Crew, roster 11
rumors.standing: Standing disclaimer: none of this is reporting. Nobody quoted here has said a word to me, every trade below is invented, and I am in the standings — five of the twelve 2027 firsts are mine, and three of them were handed over by teams I write about below. Read accordingly.
lede: The pick ledger loosened this week and I want to be careful about how much credit I take for noticing, because I am one of the five names on it. A fortnight ago nine of the twelve 2027 first-rounders sat in two pairs of hands. After Wednesday there are five holders: I have five of them, and Lovely Day, Trade Calculator Guy and Too High Safeties have two each. Somewhat Goodfellas has his own and nothing else.

That matters more than it sounds. When two men hold everything, nobody else can build a package. When five do, a 4-4 team can find a seller, and that is precisely what happened on Wednesday afternoon.

Here is the part that matters about that trade. I was the obvious buyer for D’Andre Swift. This paper said so in print last Tuesday — that I should pay the 0-7 team’s first for him. I did not do it, and a team with a worse record than mine and a thinner roster than mine went and paid its own first instead. I would like to tell you that was discipline. It was closer to inertia.

What I am hearing — and I want to mark this clearly as a read rather than anything I have been told — is that the two 6-2 teams in the West have both worked out that one of them is going to be a wild card, and neither intends to be the one that stood still. Watch that division for the next fortnight.

items.head: Five hands, not two, and that is why Wednesday happened
body: The 2027 firsts I hold belong to COME AND TAKE IT, Trade Calculator Guy, Blame spanos, the Shooters and the 0-8 roster in the East. Three of those five are winning at the moment, which is the joke on me and I have told it before. What is different this week is that there are other sellers in the market.

Lovely Day is now the interesting one. He owns his own first and the one belonging to a 4-4 team that has just mortgaged it to try to go 9-5. If that works, deucebrat holds a pick in the twenties. If the luck keeps doing to barringinjury what it has done for eight weeks, he holds something a good deal better than that. He has taken a position on somebody else’s season, which is the most sophisticated thing anybody in this league has done this year.
items.fit: Twelve 2027 firsts: five with the Crew, two each with Lovely Day, Trade Calculator Guy and Too High Safeties, one with Somewhat Goodfellas. Seven rosters hold none at all.

items.head: The 6-2 team with five quarterbacks and no tight end
body: Cheddar Bobs has 47.80 points from the tight end position across eight weeks. Last in the league by 24.20. He also has five quarterbacks on a roster that can start two of them at most. I have written about his tight end room before and I am going to keep writing about it until somebody fixes it, because he is 6-2 and this is the only thing on the roster that can cost him a January.

The version that actually clears is small. He does not need to buy the best tight end available; he needs to stop starting nothing. Out. Of. Town. Shooters. is 3-5 at 0.3 percent with the second-best tight end production in the league and no reason on earth to keep it.

deal.label: The deal that makes sense
deal.verdict: A spare quarterback for a startable tight end. It moves Cheddar Bobs’ best eleven forward by 0.46 points a week, which is small, and it moves him off a position that has produced 47.80 points all season, which is not. tdsmith23 gives up weekly scoring he has no use for and takes a 23-year-old quarterback into a rebuild that already runs through the position.

items.fit: Cheddar Bobs: 47.80 points at tight end, twelfth of twelve, 24.20 behind eleventh. Five quarterbacks rostered, 284.00 points produced, fifth in the league. Out. Of. Town. Shooters.: 155.10 at tight end, second in the league, on a roster at 0.3 percent.

items.head: Cash the tight end out before the table catches up
body: Trade Calculator Guy is 3-5 and 0.8 percent and he has one genuinely valuable asset that is not a quarterback: a 22-year-old tight end the valuation desk prices at 4.31 points a week above replacement, second-dearest at the position in this league. The same desk has him producing 2.44 a week. I flagged that gap last week and I want to advance it rather than repeat it, because the gap is the trade.

A price that far ahead of production is a selling opportunity with a clock on it. Every week he plays and does not produce, the table moves toward the box scores. igross should be shopping him to the one 6-2 roster in this league with a hole at exactly that position, and he should be doing it this fortnight.

deal.label: The deal he should be making
deal.verdict: igross converts a price he does not believe in into a 26-year-old back who starts for him immediately — his best eleven improves by 6.28 points a week, the largest single lineup swing on the board. TJWill takes the position hole off his roster for good and gives up a running back he is third in the league without. This is the one I would actually try to make if I were either of them.

items.fit: Harold Fannin: priced 4.31, producing 2.44 a week. Chase Brown: priced 3.54 on a Cheddar Bobs backfield of 365.70 points, third in the league. Trade Calculator Guy running backs: 227.60, seventh.

items.head: The new number one is tenth at the position
body: COME AND TAKE IT is first in these power rankings, has the best all-play record in the league and just filed the cleanest lineup of the season. His quarterbacks have produced 203.70 points, tenth of the twelve. In a superflex league that is not a quirk, it is a structural discount he has been getting away with because the rest of the roster is excellent.

He cannot pay in picks because he does not own any, and he cannot pay in FAAB because he has none. So he pays in receivers, which he has more of than anybody needs. Hoya Paranoia has three quarterbacks priced above 3.00 and a receiver room that is seventh in the league.

deal.label: The deal neither of them will admit to considering
deal.verdict: BADS upgrades the weakest part of a first-place roster and his best eleven gains 1.38 points a week. jlundblad gives up his third-most-valuable quarterback — he still has Caleb Williams at 4.00 — and takes back two startable bodies for a roster that has stranded 201.80 points on its bench this year. Both of these teams are going to the playoffs, which is the only real argument against it.

items.fit: COME AND TAKE IT: 203.70 quarterback points, tenth; 302.20 at receiver, sixth, with eight rostered. Hoya Paranoia: three quarterbacks priced above 3.00; 296.10 at receiver, seventh.

items.head: Four hundred points of receiver on a 2-6 roster
body: Somewhat Goodfellas has the best receiver production in the Cartel — 397.40 points, ahead of a 6-2 team — and he is eliminated. He also has $200 of waiver money he has not touched and the second-largest pick holding on the dynasty board at 11.44.

I am not going to print a deal here, and I want to be straight about why. The desk prices his best receiver at 5.92 a week, fourth in the league, and there is no package in this league inside fifteen percent of that which does not involve somebody’s best player. Every version I ran came out over thirty percent lopsided. That is the honest answer: he is holding an asset the market here cannot pay for, and he should hold it into the offseason rather than take sixty cents.
items.fit: Somewhat Goodfellas: 397.40 receiver points, first; 48.30 at running back, twelfth, against a league eleventh of 102.00. $200 of FAAB, 11.44 of pick value, and 53.5 percent of his roster price resting on men with two starts or fewer in this league.

items.head: The 0-8 roster finally moved, for eleven dollars
body: Too High Safeties spent $11 this week on two running backs that 100 Yards And Runnin had released the previous evening. That is the first money he has spent all season and I think it is more interesting than it looks: he bid $4 for one of them, lost, and came back the next day at $6 and won. Somebody is paying attention down there.

He has $247 left, the biggest budget in the league, ten picks in the 2027 draft and a 99.8 percent chance of handing me the first selection in it. I have said before that I own that pick and I will say it again because it is the single most valuable thing in this column and I did nothing to earn it except buy it in 2024.
items.fit: Too High Safeties: $247 remaining, 0-8, all-play 5-83, 99.8 percent to finish twelfth. His 2027 first belongs to Not F*cking Around Crew.

heard: Nine transactions in the Week 8 window after a week with none. One trade, two successful claims, two failed ones, four cuts. Eleven dollars. For a league six weeks from a deadline with four teams mathematically done, that is a quiet market, and quiet markets break all at once.

No manager in this league started a player the league office had ruled Out in Week 8. Ten were designated. That is the first clean week of the season and it is worth saying out loud, because this paper has spent two months naming the people who got it wrong.

100 Yards And Runnin released Corey Kiner and Eli Heidenreich at 10.17pm Eastern on the Thursday and had both claimed off him inside two days. If you are cutting depth to make room, somebody downstream is counting.

The two 6-2 teams in the West are separated by 4.86 points a game and 7.3 percentage points of division probability. The one with the better roster has the worse tight end room in the league by twenty-four points.

Lovely Day has released three quarterbacks this season and is eleventh in quarterback production. Case Keenum went on Wednesday morning, five hours before the trade. A roster that is rebuilding does not need a 38-year-old on it, but it is a reminder of what the Week 4 deal that brought him actually bought.

I will put this on the record since the paper keeps score of me: I think 100 Yards And Runnin was right to buy and wrong to pay with his own first. The pick was the one asset on that roster whose value goes up if the season goes badly. He has just removed his own hedge.

signoff.label: Last word
signoff.text: Five 2027 firsts, first on the dynasty board by 14.12 points, and seventh of twelve on the thing that decides who plays in January. I left 33.70 points on my bench on Sunday and won by thirty. Across the season it is 254.46, which is 31.81 a week and the worst number of its kind in this league. I have spent this column telling other men which of their assets they are misusing. Mine is the lineup card.

tow.label: Manager of the Week
tow.line: 96.3 percent — 175.00 scored from a roster capable of 181.80, with 6.80 points left behind across thirty men. No lineup card in this league has converted better all year, and he needed every point of it to win by 9.38.

lounge.label: The Loser’s Lounge
lounge.line: 48.10 from a ceiling of 72.30 — the lowest score filed in this league all season, by 27.66 points. In fairness the 66.5 percent is not the story: no other roster carried a ceiling below 99 this week, and his was the only one that could not have reached 73 with a perfect lineup.

court.label: Trade Grades
court.line: Four verdicts filed: one at the trade on Wednesday’s Swift-and-Waller deal, and three at four weeks on the cluster of Week 4 deals. The book reaches 123. The Addison trade’s four-week review is the one to read — a 2029 first for a receiver who has since left the roster.

faab.label: FAAB Watch
faab.line: Eleven dollars moved, all of it from the 0-8 roster, on two running backs another manager had released the previous evening. Four budgets now read zero — Raptor’s, BADS’s, barringinjury’s and CharlesRobinson’s — while DavisNuaimi sits on $247.

draft_column.byline: Mel Kiper Jr. · the board, four drafts deep
intro: Five weeks of 2026 production are in the book and the board has moved, so let me bring you up to date. Four hundred and thirty-two selections across five drafts — 240 in the 2023 startup and 48 apiece in the 2023 rookie draft, 2024, 2025 and 2026 — and every one of them graded on what it has produced in a starting lineup. Not on what I said about it at the time. Not on what the trade calculator says about it this morning.

The order of my board is unchanged and every number underneath it is not. Each of the twelve managers gained between 2.1 and 6.0 points per selection this week, which is what five more weeks of football does to a denominator that has not moved. Chasing Glory stays first at 270.7 points a pick from TWENTY picks — twenty! — and the margin to second place has widened again: 55.8 this morning against 54.4 last week. Make a fifth as many selections as the man at the bottom of this page and average more than double his return, and that is not variance, that is a scout.

Here is the thing I want on the record this week. There are five selections in the history of this league that have produced a thousand points or more, and Sunday added the fifth. Four of the five are quarterbacks and the newest is not. Two of the five are still owned by the man who called the name and three of them are not, and the two that moved — Josh Allen and Patrick Mahomes — were the first and second overall selections of the startup. In a superflex league where sixty-seven quarterbacks are rostered for twenty-four weekly slots, that is the whole market in four sentences.

1.note: Twenty selections, eight hits, 270.7 a pick — the best figure on my board by 55.8, and the margin grew again this week. Jahmyr Gibbs at 1.05 of the 2023 rookie draft added 39.20 on Sunday and crossed a thousand points: 1,006.30, fifth-most productive selection this league has ever made and the only member of that group still playing for the manager who drafted him. Jordan Love in the seventh round of the startup, 857.28, and Love has been somebody else's quarterback for a while now. Three of the twenty are still on this roster, which tells you he treats a pick as currency rather than a keepsake. The drafting is elite and the conversion is better.

10.note: Thirty-four selections, fourteen hits, fourteen retained, 214.9 a pick — second on my board and the only manager who manages volume, hit rate and retention all at once. Lamar Jackson at 1.10 of the startup for 1,063.14 is third all-time in this league and he still owns him, which in this format is rarer than the pick itself. C.J. Stroud at 1.04 in the 2023 rookie draft. George Kittle in the EIGHTH round of the startup for 606.00 is the most productive tight end anybody in this league has ever selected and Kittle plays for 100 Yards And Runnin now. The blemish stays Travis Hunter at 1.03 in 2025 on zero, and Sleeper files him at defensive back, which makes it construction rather than evaluation.

6.note: Twenty-five picks, nine hits, 205.6 a selection, third on my board. Josh Allen at 1.02 of the 2023 startup has produced 1,333.70 points, the most productive selection in the history of this league by 219.28 — and Josh Allen plays for 100 Yards And Runnin, while this roster sits eleventh in the league in quarterback production. That is the review in one sentence and it has been for three years. Now the part that is genuinely outstanding: Jeremiyah Love at 1.01 and Carnell Tate at 1.02 in 2026, 47.60 and 38.90, the two most productive picks of a forty-eight-man class, both 21 years old and both still here. Five of twenty-five retained overall. He finds them and he sells them.

7.note: Twenty-six selections, twelve hits, 199.0 a pick, fourth on my board. Joe Burrow at 1.03 of the startup for 727.14 is the anchor and he kept him. Bijan Robinson, who has delivered 93.70 points above replacement in five starts since arriving, was drafted 1.01 of the 2023 rookie draft by Somewhat Goodfellas — the best player on this roster came out of somebody else's board. Four of twenty-six still here, third-lowest retention in the league. And across twenty-six selections I cannot find a tight end worth discussing, which is precisely the slot now costing him a first-round bye.

8.note: Thirty-four picks, ten hits, 196.0 a selection, and that average is carried by two extraordinary swings rather than by breadth. Jalen Hurts at 1.04 of the startup for 1,114.42, second all-time in this league, and he still has him. Baker Mayfield in the TWELFTH round for 888.56 — more than four times what that round returns and the finest value selection this league has produced — and Mayfield now sits behind four other quarterbacks on COME AND TAKE IT's roster. Travis Kelce at 2.17 of the startup for 484.00 is still here too. Twelve of thirty-four retained. Kaleb Johnson at 1.09 in 2025 remains on zero.

11.note: Forty-eight selections, second-most in this league, twenty-four hits — three more than anybody — sixteen retained, 195.3 a pick. The volume is the identity and this week the top end finally spoke: Drake Maye, taken 1.06 in 2024, posted 45.46 on Sunday, the largest individual score anybody has managed in the Cartel this season, and sits on 622.30 for his career. Ashton Jeanty at 1.01 in 2025 is on 249.80 and is the single most valuable asset in this league on the valuation desk's numbers, and he has not been in a lineup for two weeks. Kenyon Sadiq at 1.08 in 2026 is on zero. Seven of the twelve 2027 firsts are in this drawer, so the board is about to double, and volume is already what he has most of.

2.note: Thirty picks, eleven hits, 173.8 a selection — and two still on the roster. TWO! Patrick Mahomes at 1.01 of the startup for 1,009.50, fourth all-time, and Mahomes is sitting on an 0-5 roster the model gives a 0.0% chance of January. De'Von Achane at 1.12 of the 2023 rookie draft, now on Not F*cking Around Crew's injured reserve. He evaluates adequately and he trades everything, and he owns no selection before a 2029 second, which means this board stops growing until the end of the decade.

3.note: Fifty-three picks, twenty-one hits, 167.5 a selection. Volume without return, and the recent classes are the reason: Jordyn Tyson at 1.03 and Makai Lemon at 1.05 in 2026 are both on zero and KC Concepcion at 1.07 is on 2.90. Bryce Young at 1.02 of the 2023 rookie draft for 559.36 is the hit — he traded Young, bought him back, and started Jacoby Brissett ahead of him on Sunday. Trey McBride in the TWELFTH round of the startup for 605.70 is the second-best tight end selection in league history and McBride plays for Hoya Paranoia. Ten of fifty-three retained, and no 2027 pick in any round, so the volume stops here as well.

5.note: Thirty-eight selections, twelve hits, 155.8 a pick, and EIGHTEEN still on the roster — the highest retention figure in this league by two, which tells you he believes his own evaluations more than anybody. Bijan Robinson at 1.01 of the 2023 rookie draft for 981.30 and Jaxon Smith-Njigba at 1.06 for 743.76 are both first-rate calls; he traded the first and kept the second, and Smith-Njigba gave him 22.30 on Sunday. Against that: Fernando Mendoza at 1.04, Eli Stowers at 1.10 and Omar Cooper at 1.11 in 2026 are all on zero — three first-rounders, one class, one manager, nothing. Four 2028 firsts are still to come.

4.note: Fifty-six selections, more than anybody in this league, seventeen hits, 155.3 a pick, tenth on my board. Volume has not been kind to him. Marvin Harrison at 1.01 of 2024 is on Not F*cking Around Crew now and has not started a game there; Ty Simpson at 1.09 in 2026 is on zero; twelve of fifty-six are retained. What lifts the grade off the floor is the one room nobody else in this league drafts: Brock Bowers at 1.08 in 2024 for 453.10, still here, 25.00 on Sunday, and the best tight end production in the Cartel at 147.00 — he drafted one half of that room and acquired the other. He also made the pick that produced Sam LaPorta, 2.19 in the 2023 rookie draft, 466.30, who plays for somebody else.

9.note: Twenty-nine picks, nine hits, 150.7 a selection, eleven retained — and he is 5-0, which makes this the weakest board belonging to any contender and a real finding rather than a quibble. Zay Flowers at 1.09 of the 2023 rookie draft has returned 557.00 and is still here; Quentin Johnston at 1.07 of the same draft has returned 102.00. Those are the two ends of one evening's work. He holds four 2027 selections and not one of them is a first or a second, because Not F*cking Around Crew has both. A 5-0 roster assembled almost entirely through trade is a perfectly legitimate way to build in this format. It simply does not grade on my board.

12.note: Thirty-nine picks, eleven hits, 128.3 a selection — last on my board by 22.4 — and thirteen retained. The case for optimism is narrow and genuine: three of the five most productive selections of the 2026 class are his. Denzel Boston at 1.12 on 30.10, Jonah Coleman at 2.13 on 13.30, Jadarian Price at 1.06 on 12.00 — 55.40 points, 36.7% of everything forty-eight picks have produced league-wide. He holds seven 2027 selections and not a first, because that one belongs to Not F*cking Around Crew, and at 0-5 with a 91.9% chance of finishing last it is about to be the most valuable pick in the draft.

board.head: Jahmyr Gibbs is the fifth selection in league history to clear a thousand points, and the first who isn't a quarterback
board.body: 39.20 on Sunday took him to 1,006.30. The group above him: Josh Allen 1,333.70 at 1.02 of the startup, Jalen Hurts 1,114.42 at 1.04, Lamar Jackson 1,063.14 at 1.10, Patrick Mahomes 1,009.50 at 1.01. Three of those four went in the first five picks of the 2023 startup and two of the four have changed hands since — Allen, drafted by Lovely Day and now carrying 100 Yards And Runnin's superflex, and Mahomes, drafted by COME AND TAKE IT and now sitting on an 0-5 roster. Gibbs went 1.05 of the 2023 rookie draft to Chasing Glory and is the only man in the five playing for the manager who picked him.

board.head: Forty-eight picks, 151.0 points, and 141.9 of them belong to two managers
board.body: Jeremiyah Love at 1.01 on 47.60 and Carnell Tate at 1.02 on 38.90 are Lovely Day's. Denzel Boston at 1.12 on 30.10, Jonah Coleman at 2.13 on 13.30 and Jadarian Price at 1.06 on 12.00 are Too High Safeties'. That is 94.0% of a whole rookie class sitting on two rosters the model prices at 0.2% and 0.0%, and the other ten managers have managed 9.10 points from the thirty-seven picks they made between them, of which Antonio Williams, taken 2.14 by 100 Yards And Runnin, accounts for 3.60. Every year in this league the class lands on the teams who needed it least and every year it is treated as bad luck rather than as the draft order working exactly as designed.

board.head: Nine first-rounders are still on nothing, and the 2026 class owns seven of them
board.body: Two are hangovers from 2025: Travis Hunter, taken third overall, whom Sleeper files at defensive back and who therefore cannot score a point in this format, and Kaleb Johnson, ninth overall, who simply has not. The remaining seven are all 2026 — Tyson third, Mendoza fourth, Lemon fifth, Sadiq eighth, Simpson ninth, Stowers tenth, Cooper eleventh. Three of them were Somewhat Goodfellas' calls and two were Out. Of. Town. Shooters'. Seven blanks out of a twelve-man first round in the second week of October is perfectly normal and nobody should be alarmed by it. Seven blanks next October would mean the class never happened.

board.head: The two best tight end selections in league history went in the eighth and twelfth rounds, and neither man kept his
board.body: George Kittle, round 8 of the 2023 startup to Hoya Paranoia, 606.00 points — the most productive tight end anybody in this league has ever drafted. Trey McBride, round 12 of the same draft to Out. Of. Town. Shooters., 605.70. Kittle now plays for 100 Yards And Runnin and McBride for Hoya Paranoia, which is to say the man who found him sold him and then bought the other one. Travis Kelce went 2.17 for 484.00 and sits at 37 on a 1-4 roster. The one top-end tight end in this league still owned by the manager who drafted him is Brock Bowers, 1.08 in 2024. Four hundred and thirty-two selections and that is the list, in a format that pays a premium at the position and in which the two worst rooms belong to teams at 99.8% and 80.4% to make the playoffs.

board.head: The fifth round of the startup still beats the fourth, and the twelfth beats the eleventh by a hundred and twenty-two
board.body: The 2023 startup returns 835.6 a pick in the first round, 617.8 in the second, 491.0 in the third, and then it stops behaving like a draft. The fourth round averages 374.0 and the fifth 411.4. The eighth comes in at 370.1, which is the fourth round again, and the eighteenth at 172.6, which beats the eleventh, the thirteenth and every round that follows it. The eleventh collapses to 81.1 and the twelfth recovers to 203.2, and the reason is two names: Baker Mayfield went to Trade Calculator Guy in that round and Trey McBride went to Out. Of. Town. Shooters. in it. No line can be drawn through any of that. The useful reading is narrower: after the eighth round of a twenty-round startup there is no curve at all, only a scatter with a few live pockets in it, and the two men who reached into those pockets sit fifth and eighth on this page, which is a lesson of its own.

sunday.title: Sunday Brief
lede: The bye map is clean. Houston, New Orleans, the Giants and San Francisco are all idle, and across all twelve Cartel lineups not a single slot points at one of them — Nico Collins, Christian McCaffrey, Malik Nabers, Alvin Kamara and George Kittle are all sitting exactly where a week off says they should sit. Fix This First has nothing to say.

The league office is where it went wrong. Four starters carry an Out designation on this week's injury report and all four are still in lineups two hours from kickoff. Lovely Day owns half of them: RJ Harvey (knee) at running back and Carnell Tate (shoulder) at receiver, both ruled out, both did not practice, and both replaceable from a bench holding D'Andre Swift, Jacory Croskey-Merritt, Joshua Palmer and Troy Franklin. Chasing Glory has DeVonta Smith (hamstring) in a receiver slot, and the only healthy answer behind him is Ryan Flournoy — Rashid Shaheed is also out and Tank Dell is idle. Somewhat Goodfellas has Tyjae Spears (knee) at running back and nothing behind him at all.

calls.head: A.J. Brown never practiced, and BADS cannot afford the coin flip
calls.body: Brown is Questionable with an ankle and took no part in practice on any day this week. Sixth in receiver scoring is not where BADS is hurting, and a 5-2 record absorbs a quiet afternoon from most opponents. This is not most opponents. 100 Yards And Runnin is the closest matchup on the board by three-week form, 141.37 against 140.57, a gap of under a point where no other pairing this week is inside four. Cooper Kupp and Jerry Jeudy are both on the bench and both healthy. A receiver who has not practiced since last Sunday is a guess; this is not the week to take one.

calls.head: Blame spanos can take the floor and still win
calls.body: Breece Hall (quadricep) and Dalton Kincaid (chest) are both Questionable and both practiced limited, which is the designation that tells you least. rkobeb2000 is 4-3 at 70.1 percent to reach the playoffs, and he draws Lovely Day — the lowest-scoring team in the league at 98.80 a week, and the team with two ruled-out starters still on the field. Brian Robinson and Michael Mayer are the dull versions of both slots. When the opponent is scoring under a hundred, ceiling is not what you need.

calls.head: Cheddar Bobs is first in the league and last at tight end
calls.body: Jakobi Meyers is Questionable with a hamstring, did not practice, and is holding the second flex. TJWill is 6-1, top of the power ranks, and twelfth of twelve in tight end scoring — while Evan Engram sits on his bench in a league that pays a tight-end premium wherever you start one. The flex will honor that bonus. Swapping a receiver who has not practiced for a tight end who has is close on talent and not close at all on scoring format.

calls.head: Somewhat Goodfellas has to rebuild two slots, not one
calls.body: Spears is out and eloper's only other running back is CJ Donaldson, who is on New Orleans' bye. That makes this structural rather than a swap: Austin Ekeler moves from the superflex into the vacant running back slot and Fernando Mendoza takes the superflex, which is the only arrangement that puts ten live players on the field. eloper owns the best receiver room in the Cartel and the worst running back room — first and twelfth — and at 1-6 the season is already answered, but a zero is still a zero.

wire.line: Running back, unrostered. The direct answer to the hole Spears leaves in Somewhat Goodfellas, and eloper has not spent a dollar of his $200 all season.
Running back, unrostered. Same vacancy, same price — and the one to take if Estime goes first.
Running back, unrostered. Out. Of. Town. Shooters. starts Jordan Mason and J.K. Dobbins with one healthy back behind them and sits eighth in running back scoring.
Quarterback, unrostered. Superflex cover for Somewhat Goodfellas, whose only backup quarterback not on a bye this week is Mendoza.

watch: George Pickens and D.J. Moore are both Questionable with shoulders and both practiced limited for Chasing Glory. With Smith already out, Raptor could be three deep in receiver trouble against the best team in the league.
Colby Parkinson is Questionable with a rib and did not practice, and he is in Too High Safeties' second flex. At 0-7 it costs DavisNuaimi nothing but the zero.
Treylon Burks is Questionable with a foot in Lovely Day's first flex — a third problem on a team that has not fixed its first two.
Matthew Golden, Questionable with a shoulder, is eloper's third receiver. If he sits too, the rebuild above gets harder.
sunday.signoff: Four ruled-out starters are sitting in lineups that can still be changed. Change them.

initial.verdict: Chasing Glory buys back its own 2027 first for Marvin Harrison, a 24-year-old the Crew had just acquired and flipped in three weeks. Getting your own pick back is rarely a bad outcome; paying a young No. 1 receiver for it is the part that will age.

4wk.verdict: Four weeks on, the pick has not been used and Marvin Harrison has not started a game for Not F*cking Around Crew. Chasing Glory is now 95.3% to qualify, so the first-rounder it bought back is heading for the twenties — and the Crew paid for that privilege with a 24-year-old receiver it keeps behind five others.

initial.verdict: The defining deal of the offseason. Somewhat Goodfellas collected three 2028 firsts, a 2027 third and Jordan Addison for one running back. Blame spanos got the best pure runner in the league at 24 and no 2028 draft to fall back on.

4wk.verdict: Bijan Robinson has returned 93.70 points above replacement in five starts for Blame spanos, the largest figure attached to any deal in this league's 2026 book. Somewhat Goodfellas paid with Jordan Addison, three 2028 first-round picks and a third, then moved Addison on inside a month; the picks are the entire case for his side and none of them can be graded before 2028.

initial.verdict: A one-way move of a fifth-round-profile rookie receiver. Small enough that the only real cost is roster space.

4wk.verdict: Nothing to grade and nothing coming. Chimere Dike has not started for Chasing Glory and the other side of the ledger is empty in the file. After four weeks this remains a roster-trimming exercise that happened to be filed as a trade.

initial.verdict: A 2029 third for a 2029 second, three years out. Both sides are trading paper nobody can value yet.

4wk.verdict: A 2029 second against a 2029 third, with three seasons to run before either becomes a name. Not F*cking Around Crew holds the better end on the valuation desk's pick table and will not find out for a very long time whether that mattered.

initial.verdict: Age for age: Mark Andrews at 31 and a rookie receiver, against Xavier Worthy at 23 and a developmental wideout. Hoya Paranoia took the younger half of a dynasty trade, which is usually the right half.

dynasty_column.byline: By Roy Cowgirl · A current NFL broadcaster · Name withheld at the writer’s request
intro: The board barely moved, and the one thing that did tells you more than the order does. A 4-4 team sent its own first-round pick to the team at the bottom of this table. That’s 1.52 points of price going from third place to twelfth. Neither of them changed rank. That’s how little a single first is worth against what these rosters already hold — and anybody telling you a pick is a franchise asset in a twelve-team superflex hasn’t looked at a table like this one.
Not F*cking Around Crew is first again, by 14.12. Hoya Paranoia second. 100 Yards And Runnin third even after the trade, because two veterans came back the other way and the desk still prices them.

The number worth your time is ninth. COME AND TAKE IT is first in the power rankings and ninth here. An eight-place gap, the widest divergence on the board and the widest anybody’s had all season. He holds 26.13 and not one point of it is a draft pick. He owns nothing in 2027, nothing in 2028, nothing in 2029. He’s the best team in this league right now and there’s no second act.

That’s not a criticism. It’s a description. There’s a perfectly good way to play this format where you spend everything on the present and accept that the bill lands in two years, and he’s playing it well. But the next time somebody tells you the first-place team is a dynasty, show them that line.

The reverse case is seventh and eighth, tied to the cent at 30.14. Chasing Glory and Somewhat Goodfellas hold exactly the same amount in opposite forms: 29.78 of Chasing Glory’s is players and 0.36 is picks, while Somewhat Goodfellas has 18.70 in players and 11.44 in picks. The order between them breaks on players over picks, which is the right way round. One of them is 6-2. One of them is eliminated.
Now the part I’m obliged to tell you. A ranking that hides its soft spots is worth less than one that prints them.

Twenty-three point two percent of every point of value on this board belongs to men with two starts or fewer in this league. Nearly a quarter. I don’t know what they’re worth, and the model doesn’t either — it’s reading a curve, not evidence. Somewhat Goodfellas is the extreme at 53.5 percent, so over half of what he owns is guesswork. Out. Of. Town. Shooters. 45.2 percent. Too High Safeties 43.1 percent. COME AND TAKE IT 31.5 percent, which earns that ninth place a little charity.

And there’s a specific one. Robinson’s column has a 22-year-old tight end priced at 4.31 a week and producing 2.44. That number’s on my table too. It’s the single largest gap between price and evidence anywhere in this league, and I’m not going to pretend my own board has corrected for it. It hasn’t. So if you’re using fifth place to argue that Trade Calculator Guy is in decent shape, a quarter of his price is unproven and the dearest piece of it is that man.

These prices are also four weeks old, and the board says so on its face. Nothing that happened in October is in them. That includes the quarterback who changed hands at the end of it and the two veterans who moved last Wednesday.

Zero percent of the holding clears replacement on four of these rosters — igross’s, DavisNuaimi’s, tdsmith23’s and deucebrat’s. I checked, because it reads like a bug. It isn’t. Not one player on any of the four is producing above replacement at his position right now. Three are tearing down on purpose. The fourth is 3-5 and thinks he’s still in this.
